name: US recession risk
summary: Sahm recession indicator 0.00 for October; yield curve +0.25 on 10 Nov; jobless claims at a one-year low
state: The real-time Sahm rule indicator was 0.00 for October, far from the 0.5 trigger (FRED). The 10y–2y Treasury curve was +0.25 on 10 Nov, down from +0.32 a day earlier. Initial jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, keeping the four-week average at 194,750, its lowest in a year (FRED).
for_you: US labour market data show no recession signal. A rise in unemployment would usually show up first in weekly jobless claims.
why: A US recession drags world trade, earnings and jobs; it is the single biggest swing factor for the global cycle.
drivers: Labour market, consumer spending, credit conditions, rates and fiscal policy.

rubric.alert: Sahm ≥ 0.50, or two consecutive negative GDP quarters, or NBER declares recession.
rubric.watch: Sahm 0.30–0.49, or one negative GDP quarter, or payrolls negative in a release.
rubric.normal: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.
